title: Grade 10 Social Science — Political Parties & Mixed Review
description: Political parties, democracy, and mixed review of history, geography, economics
subject: social-science

questions.question: Political parties are essential to democracy because they:
options: Ensure the ruling party wins every election
Contest elections, form governments, pass policies, and give voters organised choices between different visions
Remove the need for elections
Represent only the interests of the wealthy
questions.explanation: Political parties: (1) contest elections, (2) put forward policies, (3) form and run governments, (4) play opposition role, (5) shape public opinion. Without parties, individual candidates cannot organise government.

questions.question: The main challenge facing political parties in India today is:
options: Too many parties participating in elections
Dynastic politics, corruption, lack of internal democracy, and criminalisation of politics
Too few voters participating
Excessive government regulation of parties
questions.explanation: Key challenges: dynastic succession (only family members get top positions), corruption, lack of internal democracy (party members cannot choose leaders freely), and candidates with criminal records.

questions.question: A 'national party' in India is recognised based on:
options: Having the most seats in Parliament
Meeting Election Commission criteria — at least 6% of votes in 4+ states or winning 2% of Lok Sabha seats from 3+ states
Being in power at the Centre
Having offices in all state capitals
questions.explanation: The Election Commission of India recognises national parties based on vote share (≥6% in 4+ states and 4+ seats in Lok Sabha) or seats won (≥2% of LS seats from ≥3 states). Currently: BJP, INC, AAP, BSP, CPI(M), NCP, NPP.

questions.question: The right to vote in India is exercised:
options: Only by people with education
By all Indian citizens aged 18 and above (universal adult franchise)
Only by people who pay taxes
Only by men
questions.explanation: India has Universal Adult Franchise — every citizen aged 18+ has the right to vote regardless of caste, class, religion, gender, or education. This right was granted from the 1950 Constitution (not progressive — immediate from the start).

questions.question: The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22) asked Indians to boycott:
options: Only British goods
Government schools, courts, titles and honours, legislative councils, and British goods
Only salt
Military service only
questions.explanation: Non-Cooperation Movement: boycott of (1) government-run schools/colleges, (2) law courts, (3) British titles and honours (people returned OBE etc.), (4) legislative councils, (5) foreign goods. Also hartals (strikes).

questions.question: The Mineral-based industry located near raw material sources in India is:
options: Textile industry (cotton mills)
Iron and steel industry (near iron ore and coal deposits)
Software industry
Pharmaceutical industry
questions.explanation: Iron and steel is a weight-losing industry (raw materials are heavier than finished product) — located near iron ore, coal, limestone, and water (Jharkhand-Odisha-Chhattisgarh belt: Jamshedpur, Rourkela, Bhilai).

questions.question: The Green Revolution in India primarily benefited which crops?
options: Cotton and jute
Wheat and rice (through high-yielding variety seeds, fertilisers, and irrigation)
Pulses and oilseeds
Tea and coffee
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution (1960s-70s) introduced HYV seeds, fertilisers, and irrigation — primarily for wheat (Punjab, Haryana) and rice (Punjab, Tamil Nadu). It made India self-sufficient in foodgrains.

questions.question: Globalisation in economics refers to:
options: Making all countries speak the same language
Integration of economies through free movement of goods, services, capital, and ideas across national borders
Only international trade in physical goods
Colonisation of poor countries by rich ones
questions.explanation: Globalisation = integration of the world economy: trade in goods/services, movement of capital (FDI), sharing of technology, and cultural exchange across borders. Enabled by technology, cheaper transport, and liberalisation.

questions.question: NREGA (National Rural Employment Guarantee Act) guarantees:
options: Free education for all children
100 days of wage employment per year to every rural household willing to do unskilled work
Free housing for all BPL families
Reservation in government jobs
questions.explanation: NREGA (2005), now MGNREGS, guarantees 100 days of unskilled manual work to every rural household per year at minimum wages. It is a demand-driven employment guarantee scheme.

questions.question: The 'Champaran Satyagraha' (1917) was Gandhi's first in India and was against:
options: The salt tax
The forced cultivation of indigo by peasants under the tinkathia system
The partition of Bengal
British tax on cloth
questions.explanation: In Champaran (Bihar), Gandhi led the first satyagraha in India (1917) against the tinkathia system — planters forced peasants to cultivate indigo on 3/20 of their land at a fixed low price. It was his first major success in India.

questions.question: Consumer rights in India are protected by the:
options: Indian Penal Code
Consumer Protection Act (1986, updated 2019)
Companies Act
Trade Union Act
questions.explanation: The Consumer Protection Act (1986, strengthened in 2019) protects buyers of goods and services. It established consumer forums (district/state/national), and gives consumers rights to safety, information, choice, redressal, and education.

questions.question: The National Food Security Act (2013) ensures:
options: Exports of food from India
Subsidised food (rice at ₹3/kg, wheat at ₹2/kg) to two-thirds of India's population through the PDS
Free meals at all government offices
Only organic farming
questions.explanation: NFSA 2013: provides highly subsidised grain to 67% of India's population — 50% of urban and 75% of rural. Poorest families (Antyodaya) get 35 kg/month; priority households get 5 kg/person/month.

questions.question: The Deccan Riots (1875) in Maharashtra were directed against:
options: British colonial administrators
Local moneylenders (sowcars) by peasants crushed by debt and dispossession
Indigo planters
The Nizam of Hyderabad
questions.explanation: The Deccan Riots (Pune district, 1875): Maratha peasants attacked moneylenders (baniyas/sowcars), destroying account books and debt bonds. They resented exploitation through high interest and land dispossession.

questions.question: Federalism in India means:
options: All power is with the central government
Power is divided between the Union (Centre) and the States, with both having specified areas of authority
States are fully independent from the Centre
Only states make laws
questions.explanation: India's federal structure (Part XI, Constitution): Union List (97 subjects), State List (66 subjects), Concurrent List (47 shared subjects). The Centre has residual powers. India is called a 'quasi-federal' state.

questions.question: India's location advantage (time zone) in the global information technology services sector is that:
options: India has the cheapest technology
India's time zone (IST = UTC+5:30) complements US/European business hours — allowing round-the-clock service
India has the fastest internet speeds
India is geographically central to all continents
questions.explanation: When the US East Coast ends business (5PM), it is 3:30 AM in India — so Indian IT teams work during US night, giving 24-hour service. This time zone advantage helped India's BPO/IT services boom.
